answer: Each claimant stakes a 70-credit bond and files one sparrow song from its territory, with a quill-inked transcription of its phrases. An auditor recomputes the phrases from the sparrow dialect table and timestamp; a mismatch or reused recording burns the bond. The fee starts at 39 credits; the kth identity pays 39+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7032 and 1000 fakes pay 3,535,500 plus 70,000 locked. An honest agent files once, pays 39, and reclaims its bond. A rented-song ring fails because each recording carries a key-bound territory stamp, and the nadir-hour chorus check exposes dubbed audio.
